top_signal.title: NYC commercial landlord says I’m month-to-month after intentionally not countersigning lease, while repeatedly changing settlement terms. Is her 30-day notice valid?
top_signal.summary: I have a small biz in BK, NY, and I rent a commercial studio space in Brooklyn and I’m trying to understand what my actual legal position is before this turns into a holdover case.   The situation is messy, but I have everything in writing.   Earlier this year, my landlord sent me a new lease for  March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 . The rent in that document was $4,500/month. I signed it through DocuSign and returned it. She never countersigned it.   She has now admitted to me in writing that she  intentionally did not sign the lease because I owed money .   The lease rider does contain a clause saying the lease is not binding until the landlord executes and delivers it, so I understand that is an issue. At the same time, after February she continued letting me occupy the space, continued accepting payments, continued treating me as a tenant, and her Buildium management portal showed my tenancy ending  2/28/27  and was charging me  $4,000/month .   Now she is saying there is “no lease” and that I am simply a commercial month-to-month tenant.   On August 26 she had a  30-Day Notice to Quit  served on me, terminating the alleged month-to-month tenancy effective September 30.   What I’m confused about is whether she can simply declare the tenancy month-to-month when her own conduct and records have treated it differently.
